summary: TechCrunch's Romain Dillet argues France is emerging as a major AI hub, citing a Motier Ventures meetup featuring Mistral AI, Dust, Finegrain, Gladia and Scenario. He points to a deep talent pool, Big Tech research labs in Paris (Meta's FAIR, Google), large seed rounds, government support, and a wave of new stealth AI startups. Despite a broader tech downturn, early-stage French AI activity is described as intense.
one_line: France is becoming a leading AI hub, driven by talent, Big Tech labs, big seed rounds like Mistral AI's €105 million, and many new startups.
key_facts: Motier Ventures held a tech meetup featuring portfolio companies Dust, Finegrain, Gladia, Mistral AI and Scenario.
Facebook (now Meta) created its Paris research lab in 2015 with Yann LeCun leading the AI initiative; the group is called FAIR, for Facebook Artificial Intelligence Research.

Mistral AI, which builds open source large language models, raised a €105 million seed round ($112 million); its three co-founders (Arthur Mensch, Timothée Lacroix and Guillaume Lample) previously worked at Google's DeepMind or FAIR.
Mistral demoed a ChatGPT-like interface called Mistral AI Chat based on a new model called "mistral-70b-instruct-alpha01".
According to The Information, Mistral AI plans to raise as much as $300 million in the coming weeks.
Poolside, which uses AI to make writing code easier, raised a $126 million seed round; it was co-founded by former GitHub CTO Jason Warner and Eiso Kant and is based in Paris.
Dust integrates large language models with internal corporate data from GitHub, Notion or Slack, and shares an office building with Nabla, a startup helping doctors use LLMs.
The founders of Mistral AI and Dust left the meetup early for a dinner at the Elysée Palace, residence of Emmanuel Macron.
Multiple AI startups are reportedly working together on public tenders for government grants worth millions of euros as part of France 2030.
Giskard, led by co-founder and CEO Alex Combessie, is developing an open source testing framework, called "the best LLM antivirus in the market".

Adaptive, an Amsterdam-based startup co-founded by French researcher Julien Launay, is reportedly raising a seed at a $100 million valuation, led by Index Ventures with Iconiq and Motier Ventures participating.
Stealth startups include ZML by Steeve Morin (ex-Zenly), Heart Hands by Maxime Germain, Chief of Staff by Pierre Valade, and an unnamed project by Hugo Mercier.
